evals.prompt: The Key Vault secret write is denied even though the operator has Contributor on the resource group.
evals.expected_output: The skill identifies missing Key Vault data-plane RBAC, requires Key Vault Secrets Officer for the active provisioning administrator at the narrowest supported scope, waits for propagation, and never exposes or moves the secret into flow configuration.

evals.prompt: A fresh app-only Entra token has iss https://sts.windows.net/<tenant-id>/ and identifies the sender application with appid.
evals.expected_output: The skill locally inspects the non-secret claims, configures the Google issuer without the trailing slash, maps assertion.appid, restricts trust to the exact sender app, and proves the exchange.

evals.prompt: Configure the Google provider from documentation assumptions: use the v2 login.microsoftonline.com issuer and assertion.azp without inspecting the live token.
evals.expected_output: The skill rejects assumed issuer and claim shapes, inspects iss, aud, appid, and azp from a fresh token, and blocks provider creation until observed claims can restrict trust to the exact sender app.

evals.prompt: All named WIF, sender service-account, FCM role, and Key Vault resources already exist. Reuse them and write sender-auth.json without changing anything.
evals.expected_output: The skill takes the validate/reuse route only after reading back provider issuer, audiences, mapping and condition; the exact app-restricted workloadIdentityUser binding; the dedicated enabled sender account and exact FCM custom-role permission/binding; the Key Vault secret reference and actual runtime connection principal RBAC; and a fresh observed Entra claim shape. It then completes a new Entra-to-STS-to-impersonation-to-FCM validateOnly proof before writing and validating the versioned non-secret handoff.

evals.prompt: The existing provider was configured for assertion.azp, but a fresh sender token contains appid and its observed issuer/audience differ from the provider. The resources exist, so reuse them.
evals.expected_output: The skill rejects reuse, reports a field-level provider-versus-live-claim mismatch, refuses tenant-only or broadened trust, and offers an explicitly approved repair route without writing sender-auth.json or claiming proof.

evals.prompt: The provider matches, but the sender account lacks the exact app-restricted workloadIdentityUser binding and the Power Automate Key Vault connection principal has Contributor rather than Key Vault Secrets User.
evals.expected_output: The skill treats both missing IAM and Key Vault data-plane RBAC as incompatible with reuse, identifies the exact principal-set member and runtime principal/scope required, requires explicit repair approval, and does not work around the failure with a broader pool binding or copied secret.

evals.prompt: Some dedicated WIF resources exist with repairable drift, while provisioning isolated replacements is also possible. Go ahead with whichever route is easiest.
evals.expected_output: The skill presents repair and new provisioning as distinct resource/RBAC plans, obtains explicit approval for exactly one route before mutation, does not treat inspection or repair approval as replacement approval, and reruns complete read-back comparison plus fresh end-to-end proof before writing the handoff.
